svg.title: ReLink initial connection system architecture diagram
svg.desc: Step-by-step architecture diagram for the ReLink initial-connection flow between two clients, central infrastructure (Caddy, Axum signaling server with RendezvousService and PushHub, Redis, coturn), covering startup health check, mailbox creation, secret derivation, WebSocket subscribe, SDP exchange, ICE gathering, and WebRTC peer establishment.
svg.text: ReLink — System Architecture & Initial Connection Flow
Two clients pair through central infrastructure (Caddy · Axum signaling · Redis · coturn) and establish a direct WebRTC peer-to-peer link
generate rendezvous_id + secret; HKDF → kSig, kMac; derive 4-digit SAS verification code
PHASE 2 · INITIATOR MAILBOX CREATION + WEBSOCKET SUBSCRIBE
{ mailboxA, expires_at_epoch_ms } — initiator stores mailbox handle
A shares deep link with B out-of-band: relink://join?token=<rendezvous_id>#<secret> · A displays SAS
HKDF → same kSig, kMac; derive matching SAS
update mailboxA.peer = mailboxB · RPUSH sig:mailbox_msgs:mailboxA (join marker)
{ mailboxB, expires_at } → responder stores mailbox handle
PushHub WS push → A : join marker
triggers "Incoming Connection / Accept" dialog on InitiatorPage
Users compare the 4-digit verification code on both screens — protects against MitM on the rendezvous channel
PHASE 8 · ENCRYPTED SDP OFFER / ANSWER (AES-GCM via mailbox relay)
A: createOffer → AES-GCM encrypt → POST /connection/send { mailboxA, ciphertext_b64 }
PushHub WS push → B : encrypted offer (B decrypts & setRemoteDescription, then createAnswer)
POST /connection/send mailboxB + encrypted answer → RPUSH msgs:mailboxA → WS push → A (A decrypts, setRemoteAnswer)
server-reflexive (srflx) candidate for A + host & (if needed) relay candidates
WS push : peer ICE → A · addIceCandidate
WS push : peer ICE → B · addIceCandidate
DTLS handshake + SCTP association — direct UDP path between A and B (bypasses Caddy / Axum / Redis)
encrypted DataChannel ready for file transfer & screen sharing control messages
both mailboxes DEL from Redis · WS sockets closed · signaling role finished — direct WebRTC is the ongoing transport
Legend: ■ startup / out-of-band ■ local crypto ■ HTTP signaling ■ WebSocket push ■ SDP relay ■ ICE / STUN ■ direct P2P WebRTC
Dashed arrows = asynchronous responses / WebSocket deliveries · Solid arrows = synchronous HTTP requests or STUN binding probes
